textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 science · Light: Shadows and Reflections · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Luminous objects make their own light, such as the Sun, a torch and a candle. Non-luminous objects like the Moon only reflect light.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Luminous objects make their own light, such as the Sun, a torch and a candle. Non-luminous objects like the Moon only reflect light.
beats.speakEn: Luminous objects make their own light, such as the Sun, a torch and a candle. Non-luminous objects like the Moon only reflect light.

beats.en: Transparent materials let light through clearly. Translucent materials transmit and scatter some light. Opaque materials block light from passing through. Light travels in straight lines.
beats.speakEn: Transparent materials let light through clearly. Translucent materials transmit and scatter some light. Opaque materials block light from passing through. Light travels in straight lines.

type: Key Concept: Luminous objects make their own light, such as the Sun, a torch and a candle.
Rule: Transparent materials let light through clearly.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 science · Light: Shadows and Reflections · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: A shadow forms where an object blocks light. Its outline depends on the object, light and screen.

beats.en: A shadow forms where an object blocks light. Its outline depends on the object, light and screen. With the light source and screen fixed, moving the object towards the source usually makes its shadow bigger.
beats.speakEn: A shadow forms where an object blocks light. Its outline depends on the object, light and screen. With the light source and screen fixed, moving the object towards the source usually makes its shadow bigger.

beats.en: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. A plane mirror forms an image of the same size, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and it shows mirror
beats.speakEn: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. A plane mirror forms an image of the same size, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and it shows mirror

type: A shadow forms where an object blocks light. Its outline depends on the object, light and screen.
Reflection is light bouncing off a surface. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
